utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The Chamber would like to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. One of the issues on our agenda -- yes, perhaps we first deal with a few documents that are now, as I understand, are now in the electronic system. I'm specifically asking your attention to whether we have complete translations when we will decide on whether to admit any of these documents. We have D14 at this moment, which is a list of members of the special police unit PJP. Any objection? If you --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I apologise. I just spilled water all over my computer monitor --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is better than on the key board, Mr. Re, I promise you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, it is the keyboard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, it's the keyboard. It could have disastrous consequences. Yes. Perhaps another way of dealing with it is that Madam Registrar prints out for all parties the list I have in front of me so that we can go through it more quickly soon. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, soon, or a bit later, Madam Registrar will provide the parties with a list I've got in front of me which is about D14 up to and including D21 and P28, 29, and P30. We'll deal with it in a quicker way if we have all received that list. Then the other matter is: How much time would the Defence need to give further oral submissions in response to the Prosecution's submissions in relation to the recording of proofing sessions?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think if delivered orally it's likely to be in the region of about an hour, slightly less perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I suggest that we don't do that now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Under those circumstances, the Chamber would prefer to receive -- although we had in mind to receive your submissions orally, to receive it on paper and -- to receive it on paper. That's for all three counsel. If the Prosecution would like to respond to the submissions made by the Defence, the Prosecution is then invited also to make these written submissions.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I apologise. The -- both parties have filed written submissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I understand the Defence wishes to respond orally to our written submissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, they were more or less invited to do it -- or they indicated that they wanted to respond because there were certain matters not put rightly, from what I understand. They wanted to correct that. We thought at that time that it might take such time if we could receive them orally, because we might have had time available today, but if it takes an hour we'd rather receive it in writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No, I understand that. The Prosecution's position is that there are -- there is one major legal error in the Defence submissions which requires correction. We're certainly happy to do it orally; however, if you look at the two binders here, this is the -- we've prepared books of authorities. So there's actually two binders full of material which -- I think we would appreciate Your Honours having a look at before --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I -- that would -- if you would make this available to the Prosecution [sic] and to the Chamber. Are these the sources that we find in the annexes, mainly that's domestic practice?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's everything. It's everything except ICTY and ICTR law. Everything else which we have referred to, domestic, international articles is collected. We've got copies for the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: All the legal stuff?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All the legal stuff is collected in one binder and we would like Your Honours to read it first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course if I would have said that you should make it available to the Prosecution, I meant to say to make it available to the Defence. Mr. Re, your new keyboard is there. If you would provide this material to the Defence, then the Defence would include it, I take it, in their response. When could we expect the written submissions, Mr. Emmerson?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Would Your Honour say Tuesday?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's fine. We have filed all this material. We just printed out for the convenience of the Court. We filed a book of authorities and a glossary. So it's all in the court system. It just takes the registry a long time to digest this stuff that's why we printed it out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I've just not seen it. Tuesday, could you make any additional written submissions in writing by Tuesday, as well? How much time would you need orally?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I would whatever time the Defence is -- I would want equality of arms here if the Defence wants an hour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Equality of arms is the following: That written submissions are expected. If, however, you would consider that you could make your submissions orally within five minutes, I would allow you to do so. The Defence certainly is -- so the choice is either orally within five minutes or in writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I misunderstand. Is Your Honour saying both sides will get five minutes because both sides are putting submissions on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, what I'm saying is you can choose either to do it orally and then you get five minutes; if you think more, then you have to do it in writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Does that apply to the Defence as well?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Defence has said they need an hour, so therefore they are instructed to file in writing, and they don't get the five minutes anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you. I hear what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. So by Tuesday, either five minutes or a written submission. That's understood. That's ordered, I would say. Then -- yes. Another matter and that is related to Mr. Re. Could the Prosecution provide the Chamber with all the documents created or used by the OTP which concerned the conduct of OTP staff in proofing sessions such as policies and procedures, other forms of guidance concerning the conduct of proofing sessions, if they do exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then we would like to receive that by Tuesday as well. The next question -- procedural issue, Mr. Re: When will the Prosecution file the corrected version of the 92 bis motion? I earlier mentioned that we had been in touch with the Prosecution in an e-mail asking for a corrected version of the 92 bis motion. When do you think you would file that?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, there's a draft of -- I just can't remember. I think I may have a draft; I'd have to check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I just can't answer it as I stand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we would like to hear from you at a later stage, preferably today, if you could find out by the next break.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then still to be done is the re-arrangement of the proposed exhibits in relation to Witness Andjelkovic. Mr. Re, when could the Chamber expect the re-arranged exhibits?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Would Tuesday be acceptable?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I -- since no Defence counsel jumps up, Tuesday is fine. Then there's another matter. There is still pending a request for a subpoena in relation to a book, and the Prosecution needed some time to find out whether the book they received is the relevant book. Are you already in a position to tell us whether you would withdraw that request for subpoena?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If Defence counsel can put on the record that that book is the one the subject of the subpoena, I will take -- I will accept that undertaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I can put on the record that the book that I handed to Mr. Re had the same title and the same authors as the book that's mentioned in his subpoena request, and that's something he can read for himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And I take it that you're not aware of any different versions of this same book?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I am not aware of any other versions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's then clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: On that basis, we do withdraw our application for subpoena.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it's on the record that you have withdrawn your request for subpoena in this respect. That was the application that was filed on the 9th of February of 2007. Yes. There's another matter not totally unrelated to the matters we discussed earlier this afternoon. The Chamber would like to -- that the Prosecution provide general and updated information about the situation for witnesses or potential witnesses in war crimes trials in Kosovo. The staff of the Chamber is aware of -- we have not read it, I immediately add to that, but our staff has, upon our request, inquired into the existence of public information that could be of interest when assessing motions for protective measures. Some titles have been brought to our attention as possible sources of information, but, as I said, we haven't read it, neither has the staff. The Defence is invited to provide such information or any material that it considers relevant on this specific issue. The Chamber will then consider whether to assign exhibit numbers on any of the material submitted, and I'm just at this moment giving some titles our attention was drawn to. Again, we haven't read it. That's an OSCE report of December 2006: "Review of the Criminal Justice System in Kosovo" with a specific first chapter on the protection of witnesses in the criminal justice system. There is an OSCE report April 2003 until October 2004: "Review of the Criminal Justice System in Kosovo." A report with a similar title covers March 2002 until April 2003. This last report deals entirely with witness protection; whereas, the earlier one I mentioned, the 2003/2004, only some pages deal with witness protection and also describes, as far as we were informed, some incidents in connection with domestic trials. The Chamber is also informed that there are -- an article has been published dealing with the issue; one of them being an article by Michael Farquhar with the title: "Witness Intimidation: A Serious Problem in Kosovo," published by the Institute for War and Peace Reporting, dated 1st of April, 2005. Another article by Jeta Xharra, I don't know whether the pronunciation is right, with the title: "Kosovo's Wild West," as we understand published by the same institute, dated 18th of February, 2005. There may well be other publications or there may well be more information available from UNMIK, UNHCR, Council of Europe, Commission of Human Rights or NGOs, including Human Rights Watch and Amnesty International. We have not fully -- we have no full survey of what exists, but the Chamber would very much like to receive as broad information as possible but focusing on this specific subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could I just ask Your Honour in what form do you want it? Do you want us to provide it -- to put it through the e-court system or to provide -- or to find this and provide it in hard copy to -- and, of course, to the Defence and the Trial Chamber, or -- as a potential marked for exhibit -- exhibit marked for identification exhibit to go into the system? Or is it for background information? Or is it relevant to witness protection issues? In what form do we take it that the Trial Chamber wants it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you find it first, then we'll inform you in what form we would like to receive it. You'll hear that early next week. Yes, Mr. Re. Do you have any idea on how much time it would take you to find this material?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honours are obviously much better informed than we are -- than I am about the existence of this matter. Perhaps if we could liaise with whoever in Chambers has identified this, which would assist us to find it, because I can't tell you how long it would take.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Isn't it more logical that you get in touch with VWS because they are the specialists in the field, I would say. And to be quite honest, I don't know whether this list I received, I haven't read any of it, whether VWS has been assisted -- assisting in creating this list, but you're encouraged to first contact VWS. If that doesn't lead to anything, then, of course, in a transparent way you can approach the Chamber staff, that is always copy to all Defence teams. Then, meanwhile, everyone has the list prepared by Madam Registrar in front of him or her. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I answer Your Honour's question? As far as D14 is concerned --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- that is a document which currently exists in English. There is available instantly a Serbian translation of it. In fact, it was originally a Serbian document -- no, I apologise in this. That is my own summary document, apparently. It's -- I was confusing that for D16. So that document, that single sheet, D14, is only in -- it's only a list of names and the name of the PJP is in Serbian on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, usually -- well, most important is that there is a copy available to the Defence in a language the accused understands, so I leave it now to you, Mr. Emmerson. May I take it, Mr. Re, that you do not insist on having a Serbian translation attached to it?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, it's in Serbian. Just a list. Are you insisting on an English translation of that list?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's a list of names, so there isn't really an English translation for the names, other than for the name of the organisation itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you could take care that at least whatever is not just name but headings or titles or what the organisation is, that at least --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- a translation limited to that. You don't have to copy again all of the names, but at least that every text attached to these names is available in the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. We'll then wait for the admission until we have got that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That can be supplied on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. D15 --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: D15 is in English. It's the investigator's report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So there's no request from the Defence's point of view to have it translated into Albanian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, for D15 just in English. That's fine as far as the Prosecution is concerned?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I have to ask other counsel, Mr. Guy-Smith and Mr. Harvey, whether they would also be -- whether they would insist on the party that tenders it, that's Defence for Mr. Haradinaj, whether you would like to have a translation available for your clients?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No, we're satisfied with the state of the record. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: So are we. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. D15, any objection? Yes, Mr. Emmerson. Then because we could decide then that that's admitted into evidence. D16.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The position with D16 is that when produced in hard copy, all we had available was the English statement producing it and the list in English as produced to us, or otherwise as obtained from the JDB. We have now found and entered into the system the Serbian or the B/C/S original. So that is now, I understand it, entered into the system accompanying that document and so that is ready for admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it's attached to the English version?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's linked to the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that would be sufficient for you, I take it. Yes. Then any -- if there are no objections, Mr. Re, or are there?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: To its admission into evidence, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Then that's admitted into evidence. I take it that if one counsel tenders a document, that I would explicitly like to hear from other counsel if they have any problems with that document to be admitted into evidence. I'm not asking that all the time, I take it that's the situation, but please alert me when you have problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: We certainly will, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we move to D17.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: D17 and D18 are both the print-outs from the International Crisis Group reports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: They were supplied by the Prosecution in hard copy. My understanding is that they have not yet been entered into the system electronically. I see -- I see the registrar nodding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it then that if Mr. Re has an electronic copy, that he provides it to you, which might make it easier to have it introduced into the system.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, that would be helpful. As far as the translation is concerned, the Haradinaj Defence does not insist on a translation into Albanian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Other Defence counsel? I see Mr. Guy-Smith nodding no, and Mr. Harvey the same. So we'll wait with a decision until the documents have been entered into the system. D19.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: D19 is the statement in English producing the list of members of the PJP in March 1999.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There is a Serbian original attached to that, and that -- both documents are entered into the system and linked and is ready for admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Any objection, Mr. Re?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then D19 is admitted into evidence. D20.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: D20 and 21 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- are the manuscript-completed hard copies of the Council for the Defence of Human Rights versions of the two statements which seem to be the genesis of the ICG documents, together with translations which at the moment are provisional only.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we wait for a final translation and we'll then decide.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I think that ball is in the Prosecution's court because it is they who have taken the view that -- that those translations need to be checked and are checking them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, because they are provisional translations. Mr. Re, when will you hear whether the provisional translation -- now, these are provisional translations prepared by whomever on behalf of the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Usually it's then not for the Prosecution to verify whether the translation is correct, but just submit it perhaps to the CLSS in order to get -- I mean, if you want to have it admitted into evidence, then we need an official translation --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and not just a provisional translation against which the Prosecution does not object. That's --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I only said what I did because Mr. Dutertre said on the record about those documents that the Prosecution was postponing its position on their admission into evidence whilst it had them checked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's their position, but that doesn't mean that --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well, we will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- we do nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We will submit them and have the translations --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Official translations.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- verified and officialised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I might interject since you've raised the issue of translation, I should inform the Chamber that there's a potential difficulty with that in the absence of an order from the Chamber with regard to these particular documents, as well as other translations. They may not be done. So we'll proceed with that. The reason I'm raising this is the exact same thing happened with a rough translation of the Norwegian documents you have before you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber will -- unless the parties would consider this improper, we'll get in touch with the CLSS to see what is needed in order to have these documents -- the translation verified or translated so that they are in the system as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm very grateful for that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- intervention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then next one we have P28, which is a photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, and P29.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, two photographs. They are not under seal, so I could say the first one, photograph Milovan Vlahovic; the second one of Milka Vlahovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: My recollection was that those documents had already been the subject of admission, but that's obviously my memory playing tricks on me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If -- Madam Registrar is the only one who's -- I do agree that we usually do that with photographs, but I don't know -- I don't remember whether we did it this time. Well, if not --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Certainly no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- admitted into evidence then they are now, at least, admitted into evidence. Then we have one exhibit, P30, under seal, which is a DNA report.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I still wonder whether that should remain under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we raised the issue before.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- it wasn't raised by the Prosecution, I think, at the time. The position is that when those documents were disclosed - and I'll be corrected from my left if I'm wrong about this - they were disclosed on terms which required them to be considered by counsel only because the names of the donors of the samples were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it was the --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: As well as genetic information. So in the long run, it's a matter for the Prosecution to decide how much assistance, given that there's going to be nobody here to interpret these documents for Your Honours, it is to have genetic information recorded and exhibited in documents before the Tribunal, but it's been marked for identification. I don't know whether it's tendered for admission. I've got no opposition to it, but I'm not sure how much --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Prosecution is invited to give it some thought on how to deal with this material, and it is completely in English. Of course, if the parties could agree on: At that day, a DNA report was made and identified remains, et cetera --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It is all agreed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay. Then perhaps to deal with it in a different way and not to have all kind of other information because I do understand that also other persons are in this report. The Chamber would like to then have an exact formulation of what exactly is agreed upon in this respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it remains marked for identification. I'm informed that P28 and P29 has been admitted for the first time today. Yes. I have no further procedural matters. Then I suggest that --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There is one further --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- very short procedural matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This afternoon after we sat, I received copies of a letter from the Prosecution responding to the Defence request from Monday for advanced notification of witnesses to be called for the following week. I haven't yet had a chance to see it but it's there. We also received a motion from the Prosecution seeking an order from the Trial Chamber that the Defence be required to give advanced notice of any exhibits it intends to deploy in cross-examination. That is firmly opposed and we are in a position to provide written submissions in relation to it, but I'm a little anxious that we're stacking up quite a lot of written submissions in quite a short period of time. And I wonder whether Your Honours would extend the period of time for it needs a considered reply --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Until --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Until the end of next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Given that we're in -- we would oppose that. Given that we are in trial it is the practice of every Trial Chamber currently sitting to -- for that order to be made and has been for some time. In our submission the Defence does not need eight or seven days effectively to respond to putting forward something opposing what is happening --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think as a matter of fact that Mr. Emmerson would have offered reply within two or three days if, as he said, there are not a lot of other issues on which the Chamber would like to receive written submissions.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I note that it's taken the Prosecution five days to respond to our request from Monday. The position is, and again, just for the record --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's keep it short. The time you asked for is granted.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I might.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: On the 14th Mr. Re was to have a discussion with the head of the Department of Justice in Kosovo regarding matters as I will call UNMIK generically --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Article 70? Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As well as any further RFAs or other matters as they relate to witnesses who are going to be called in these proceedings. I don't believe that we've had an update on that at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's an issue revisited many times, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The last update I had was a conversation, I think, with -- definitely with Mr. Guy-Smith. It might have been on Monday this week saying the two of us would and other Defence counsel would sit down and try and thrash out something we could take to UNMIK. In terms of that conversation that was in relation to a conversation Mr. Guy-Smith had with them and I rang them and there was nothing further to add. So we might be able to resolve something if we have further discussions. If I can clearly find out exactly in writing - and I think that was what was going to happen - exactly what the Defence seeks in relation to each matter, we might be able to advance it. I'm not sure we have that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith do you think you could be of any assistance to Mr. Re in this respect?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'll be more than happy to make up another list. I've had now conversations with various representatives at UNMIK. I understand what the UNMIK position is very clearly and I think that Mr. Re needs -- understands what he needs to do, but I'll help him in that regard because I really would like to get this matter resolved as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I take it that Mr. Re appreciates that very much and let's try to avoid that this becomes a never-ending story.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There's one more procedural issue in relation to written submissions and I'm now going the other way. Last week Your Honours asked us to give written submissions in on the issue of blood-feud and the notice the Defence must give by Monday. Given the amount of written work we've had to do and I do sympathise with the Defence position and now I'm giving the opposite now. We simply can't get it in by Monday. If you could give us until Friday we would be in a much better position to -- and the Defence to file those submissions, but we simply can't get it done by Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken, that was a submission which the Prosecution was going to put forth their position and then we would respond in due course. I'm more than happy to give the Prosecution as much time as they need in order to cobble together those arguments and I'll respond in due course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Despite that there was some hesitation to give you until next Friday, you are -- you take a generous position. Mr. Re, I take it that other Defence counsel agree as well. You asked until Friday. Yes, until Friday. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It simply requires then a further period of time for the Defence to respond --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, that goes without saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm not sure when Your Honour would want that response, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It also depends a bit, I think, on what Mr. Re produces.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Sometimes a fair time for a response depends on the content of what is submitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then -- yes, finally, one of the things I -- if I remember well, I missed in the submissions until now on proofing notes is any expression of whether this should be a reciprocal system, whether it would be valid for all parties. If further submissions are made, the Chamber would very much like to have the views of the parties on that included. Yes. Then, Mr. Re, any other matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The only other matter I wished to raise was in relation to the next witness's testimony, but I would like to do that in private session before the witness comes in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Then we turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, are you ready to call your next witness, which I do understand will be Drago Stojanovic? Madam Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you give evidence in this court, you're required to make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. May I invite you to make that declaration, of which the text is now handed out to you by Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic. You'll first be examined by counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Re or -- yes. Mr. Re, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Good evening, Mr. Stojanovic. Is your name Drago or Dragoslav Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Good evening to you. Dragoslav.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is your date of birth the 1st of January, 1966?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In Dubrava, the village of Dubrava.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where is that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Decani municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where is it in relation to Glodjane?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Just next to Glodjane, the end of Glodjane and the beginning of Dubrava, it actually borders on both.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you living there in 1998?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who were you living with in 1998?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: With my mother and sister.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What are their names?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And my remaining brokers and sisters. Ljubica and Dragica --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, can you tell us again the names of your mother and sister and your remaining brokers and sisters. Just list them for us.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: There was overlap; the interpreters didn't catch the first name. Could the witness please be asked to move closer to the microphone; we can barely hear him. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Counsel for Prosecution is kindly asked to switch off the small left microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We didn't get the names of your mother, sister, and family -- other family members who were living with you in 1998.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Ljubica, Dragica. In 1998, they were living with me, and the others were living in Decani, Djakovica, Belgrade, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What is your ethnic origin or your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm a Serb, a Montenegrin.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How many Serb or Montenegrin families were living in Dubrava in 1998?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Just ours.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How many Albanian families were there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: 27 of those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: And others? Other groups maybe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, none.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, there was a - how should I put it - Catholic family, a single one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: This is Catholic Albanians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is Mijat Stojanovic your brother?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where was he living in 1998?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In Belgrade, but he came over a lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who is Veselin Stijovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: My cousin.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you say "cousin," can you better describe the relationship? Is he the son of your mother's brother, for example? Or what is the relationship?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: He's the son of my mother's sister.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where was your family house in relation to Ramush Haradinaj's family house?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mine was at the far end of Dubrava, and his was at the beginning of Glodjane.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was the -- what is the approximate distance between the two houses?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: About 150 metres, give or take a metre or two.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you know Ramush Haradinaj in 1998?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And before, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How long have you known him for?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I have known him since elementary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you attend school together?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: We used to travel to school together in Rznic with all the other kids.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want to show you a photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can Exhibit P10 please be displayed in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm going to show you a map, an overhead map. While that's coming, I might just ask you: What was your occupation in 1998?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I worked at the school. I was the handyman.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Can you just have a look at this map, please, and can you see on the house -- I think the village of Dubrava actually has a red circle around it. Yes, I'm sorry. I'll withdraw that. Please don't translate that. Can you please have a look at the map in front of you. Can you see the village of Dubrava there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are you able to take a pen, which the court usher will give to you, and I want you to mark with a circle -- firstly, before you mark, just don't go any further, I'm going to ask you to mark two things on it. One is where your house was, and the other was where Ramush Haradinaj's house was. So I want you to mark your house with a circle and Ramush Haradinaj's with a cross. We could make it larger for you, if it assists. Would you like it larger?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Please make it larger.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A little, yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Even a bit more, because otherwise the markings will become unclear. This is the right size, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, perhaps you first ask the witness whether he can perhaps orient himself on this map, because otherwise I know what's going to happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Quite so.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, are you able to -- without marking, are you able to see where your house is and where Mr. Haradinaj's house is on this map? Before you mark, just tell us whether you can do that.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I just don't know how the houses are marked. What stands for the houses? The dots perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It would appear so. They would appear to be buildings?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any dispute as to whether what is the house of the Haradinajs and the house of -- is there --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I have to say on this particular map, I'm not certain. I mean, I've seen them and I've seen photographs of both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But I'm not certain on the map, and I wouldn't want to give evidence about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But I'm wondering, Mr. Re, if the parties would agree where to find that, whether the building is on the map or not, but where to find these houses. Then if pictures are there, there could be no confusion anymore. And I know that marking on maps for persons who are not used to marking on maps is usually dramatic. I'm not -- I'm not objecting, but ask you to consider reconsidering whether it makes any sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'll just ask the witness another question to see whether we can go any further.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you've heard what His Honour has said. Do you think you can work out where your house is and where Mr. Haradinaj's is? If you can't, we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It's very difficult for me to get my bearings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's move on then, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want you to describe for the Court the land your family owned.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: My family owned 8.5 hectares of land. It was a single piece of land by the road. On two sides there was a road, and on the third side was the Haradinaj estate, Haxhija Haradinaj, and then the accused's. On the fourth side it bordered on the late Nazija's estate. He sold -- the former owner sold a piece of land to us on Tapil [phoen]. So the total surface of the land was 8.5 hectares.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was it farming land?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Most of it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How many --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Most of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How many buildings were on it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: There was a house, there was a stable, a workshop, a garage, a tobacco-drying plant or a shed. There was -- and a hen-coop 16 by 3 metres. These were all solid buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And on the map in front of us, which is Exhibit P10, was your land located on the right-hand side between Gllogjan and Gramocelj? Have I accurately described where it is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Not Gramocelj.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where road are you referring --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Dubrava towards Glodjane, so that would be the last estate towards Glodjane.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Would it be near where the word "Saptej" is written on the map?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Excuse me, the word "Saptej" is written on the map two times, so this is a confusing question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There's two Saptejs. There's one underneath Gllogjan, and there's one just to the right above Dubrava.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That's one of the Saptejs. Actually, there was only one. Only there's a road leading from Glodjane to Saptej and an old road to Dubrava which also leads to Saptej.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The two roads you are talking about or you described bordering your property, which roads are they?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I can show you here, if you wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It may have reached the point where he could assist us, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could you please draw on the map the approximate boundaries of your property?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This is the Gramocelj-Glodjane road. That's the main road, this one here. It passes by my estate. Somewhere here is where my estate should be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we invite the witness then now to mark that with a pen, since he seems to have found it. Madam Usher, could you assist the witness in taking the electronic pen? Ask him to mark the boundaries of his property on the map. Witness, could you please, with the assistance of -- if you found your estate, could you please mark that -- oh, yes, I'm looking at the wrong one. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did, but I cannot pin-point my house precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: But this is about where your property was? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. I was looking at the wrong screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Might that be marked? I might get the witness to return to this map at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, this would be number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number P31, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but it still remains as it is now, so that further markings can be made. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, do you know someone called Smajl Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And who is he?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Ramush Haradinaj's uncle, that means his father's brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about Daut Haradinaj, do you know him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: He is Ramush Haradinaj's brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you know someone called Besnik Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I think that he's the uncle's son, Ramush Haradinaj's uncle, who is named Rasim. I'm not sure about the name, but I think that's the one, but I do know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you know Ramush Haradinaj's father?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What's his name?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Hilmi Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you know Idriz Balaj?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about Lahi Brahimaj?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Lahi Ibrahimaj, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you do service in the JNA at any point?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When was that and for how long?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I think it lasted for 13 months, and it was in 1986/1987.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you living in Dubrava in January, February, March 1998?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want you to tell the Trial Chamber in general terms about things that may have started to happen from January 1998 onwards in Dubrava.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean, referring to my particular case?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Militarily.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing was happening militarily. Everything was as usual.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about in your particular case? What happened to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On the 24th of March, 1998 --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can I -- before March 1998, I want to ask you about your movements and whether you were prevented from moving around on any particular occasion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: One evening, I was coming home late. It was ten past 11.00 or thereabouts. When I came to the entrance of Glodjane - which we, the locals, called the centre -- there was a store there, a tobacconist shop, I saw four armed men there. Two had hand-held rocket-launchers and two had automatic rifles. They stopped me - I was in a car - and asked to see my identification papers. They ordered me to step out of the car. They searched my car several times. All the lights in the village were off. I expected that someone will appear from the neighbours. These men were armed. They had Balaclavas on their heads. After the search, they talked among themselves what they would do with me. One of them said that they had to ask their commander. At that moment, a green Mercedes taxi appeared from Decani, on the road from Rznic to Decani. They stopped him some 50 metres from me, checked him, and let him go, and he proceeded towards Saptej. They questioned me whether I had a brother working in the police, whether I knew anything in detail about the police. I responded by saying that I didn't know anything, and then the four of them discussed something and said that they had to ask for instructions what to do about me, and they had to ask their commander. One of them was standing behind me. He fired one bullet from his pistol, but I didn't notice this until I heard this shot being fired. Shortly afterwards, perhaps ten minutes, a man appeared from Glodjane but the road leading from Dubrava. He stopped a little further away, about 50 metres away, in a dark alley. They discussed something, I couldn't hear what they were talking about, and then the man came back. He took out a note pad from his pocket and told me to write something in that note pad in terms that I had been stopped by the Kosovo Liberation Army. That was the first time I heard about it, that the Kosovo Liberation Army had stopped me, that they hadn't mistreated me, and that they treated me well. I wrote all this down. Finally he told me to sign it, which I did, and then they told me I was free to go. And they told me, Don't be afraid. You can go. When I went back into the car, one of them called me again and said, Stop, calm yourself. He took out a packet of LM cigarettes, gave me a cigarette. He lit it for me and said that I was free to go, and I left.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you know any of those people, the ones who'd stopped you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I couldn't recognise them because it was both dark and they had these Balaclavas, and I could only see their eyes and their mouths.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What language were they talking?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: They spoke Albanian, but their accent was similar to that spoken by people from Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you speak Albanian?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you write Albanian -- read and write Albanian as well?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Now it's a little bit difficult, but at the time it was all right because I constantly used that language. I was living among Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: So this paper you had to sign or you signed also was written in Albanian, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had to write it in Albanian. I used Latin alphabet --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... write yourself, yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I put the pad on the roof of the car and wrote it down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, perhaps at a later stage you pay attention to page 78, lines 10 to 13, which is difficult to follow in terms of geography.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I will do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'll ask you to return to the map in a moment, Mr. Stojanovic, but first: When did this occur in relation to the -- how long before the incident on March the 24th you're going to tell us about did this occur?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date, but it was less than a month.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you make a report to any authorities about what had happened?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Which authorities and when?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: To the police station in Rznic, the very next morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you file a written report or did someone take a statement or what happened?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: One of the policemen took my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is the exhibit still on the screen that the witness can have a look at?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What I want you to do is if you can look back at the computer screen, the monitor, are you able to see on the screen where it was that you were stopped when this incident occurred?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Just give me a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes, I also wanted to ask you. You said you came to the entrance of Gllogjan. There was a store there, a tobacconist shop.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. There was a store at the corner, and this is the entrance to Glodjane and the road leading to Saptej. This is where the crossroads is between the road leading to Dubrava and to Saptej.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Perhaps if you could mark with an X on the map if you can see the spot where it was that you were stopped?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: If I may ask --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If this is the road to Saptej, then I can do that, this one here. From Rznic to Glodjane, so it's there in the centre where this crossroads is, where the road leading to Dubrava is. So that's the crossroads.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: I take it you were coming from Rznic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, from Rznic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: That entrance, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It happened at this crossroads.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: And this was at the crossroads or very close to the crossroads?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely on the crossroad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you think you could mark it -- I think we know where the crossroads are from your description, but do you think -- are you able to mark it with an X? Even if you can't fit it on the map, are you able to put an X or maybe an arrow pointing to it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It's here, but now there's a lot of colour here. This is the crossroads.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For the Chamber, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, you were going to tell us before about something that happened in, I think you said, the 24th of March. What was that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On the 24th of March, I went to work in the morning. That's the period when I was working at the school. It was between 10.00 or 11.00 when my mother called me and told me that something strange was going on and that there was shooting. I left my work-place and came -- and went home. When I arrived, I saw many policemen and I heard the shooting. There were shots coming from the Haradinaj house and from this other direction. I saw a wounded policeman lying on the road some 200 metres away; that was Miodrag Otovic. The police were trying to recover his body while the shots were still being fired, and it looked like a war zone. It lasted the whole day. When I arrived home, I asked one of the policemen on the road what was happening, and he told me that there were 24 armed men who had wounded the policemen. The fighting lasted until about late afternoon. The police managed to move them. Around 3.00 or 4.00 in the afternoon, a helicopter came and air-lifted the policeman. I think there were one or two helicopters. They took him to Pristina, and the action was still in progress, and I couldn't see what was actually happening from my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to ask you to pause there. You said a moment ago there were shots coming from the Haradinaj house. Was that Ramush Haradinaj's house or some other Haradinaj house?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: From Ramush Haradinaj's house, as well as the house of his cousin next to him and also from his cousin's stable, from the old house, and from the border next to my property. Two shells were fired against my house. One hit a plum tree and exploded in the yard, and the other one missed and passed between the house and the stable and landed further afield.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You referred a moment ago to fighting. Who was the fighting between, were you able to see?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I couldn't see. Being a civilian, I was barred from going out and it was dangerous. There was shooting, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who barred you from going out?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The police.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: From which direction did the two shells come?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: From Hilmi and Haxhija Haradinaj's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who else was in your house with you when this was occurring?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: My mother and my nephew, my brother's son.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How long did you remain in your house for?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: We remained until the evening. I would venture out into the yard occasionally because the cattle was loose and I had to gather it together, but we didn't dare go beyond our yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What happened -- where did you go in the evening?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In the evening there was a man, probably a commander because he had a rank, came to our house and told us that it was unsafe for us to remain there. He explicitly said that Ramush Haradinaj and his group were armed, that anything could happen, and that it would be best for us to leave and go with them. We left our house, all our belongings. I started my car, and they were -- they drove to Djakovica and I joined them in the convoy to Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: This commander, from what organisation was he?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Police.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did you go in Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I first went to the Secretariat of the Interior where we were supposed to give statements about the event. After that, I went to my brother's. I had no other place to go to.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Have you lived in your house in Dubrava since that date?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I only went from time to time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about your family? Have your family lived in the house since that date?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No, no one. The following day, I went there to see the house and the cattle. I fed the cattle, and we would then occasionally come, but we never continued living there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was the name of your brother who you lived with or went to stay with in Decani -- I'm sorry, did I say "Decani," I mean Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Decani.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I take the question back. You said you went to stay with your brother. Where was your -- what was your brother's name and where was your brother's place?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: We didn't live with him, we just spent the night there. He had a flat in the centre of Djakovica. It was a rented flat.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did you and your mother stay after leaving your house on the 24th of March, 1998?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The following day we went to Decani, asked for aid from the municipality. They gave us shelter in some barracks belonging to the monastery estate.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm so sorry to interrupt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I heard a name which doesn't appear on the transcript when asked the identity of the brother, and I wonder if Mr. Re could just simply clarify - it didn't come up on the transcript, it said it on the tape - what the names of the family members are so that we can have it clear?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your brother's name, the one you stayed with overnight, what was that name?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Predrag Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: A few moments ago, you told the Chamber that you went back from time to time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. The next day, I went on my own.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did anything happen on that next day when you went on your own?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Not to me personally, but I did see some degree of activity. My neighbours had brought over journalists to take pictures of the houses, and then the next day I read reports about that in the papers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, the witness has testified that among his neighbours was the Haradinajs, but therefore I'd like to see clarification on which neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Which neighbours are you talking about when you say: "The neighbours had brought over journalists to take pictures"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Ramush and Qamil Haradinaj, I'm talking about the Haradinaj family now. I didn't see Ramush there, but they did go to his house. Qamil and Beko came with them, as well as Besim; those were the ones I knew. There were other locals there, not just the Haradinajs. There were many of them there. There was a journalist -- not really a journalist, rather, a painter from Detane called Cacan. He was a professional decorator, but he was the man holding the camera and he was the one who took most of the pictures, including one of my home while I was looking on from my garden.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you return to your home in April 1998?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: To stay, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: To go back. Not to stay but to go back.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, I just went to check on my cattle. It was all open. I live in the countryside. We had our own livestock. We had to check on our farm every now and then.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was there a particular occasion you went back with other people and something happened?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On the 18th of April, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who did you go there with?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: With my brother Mijat and my aunt's brother Veselin Stijovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where were you coming from?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: From Baboloc.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: By what means were you travelling? Were you driving?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I was driving my own car, a Mazda 626. Mijat and Veselin arrived in their Lada station wagon.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Approximately what time of day? Was it morning? Afternoon? Evening?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: About 8.00 or 9.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why did you go there -- I'm sorry, you've told me that. What did -- what happened when you got there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When we got there, the two brothers went into the house to get some basic necessities because over in Decani we had nothing, next to nothing. Suddenly shots were being fired at us from the Haradinaj household. We were scared, and we ran into the house and locked the door. Every now and then, I would go to the window facing the terrace to see what was going on. I thought this had just been an attempt to intimidate us. But in the meantime, I realised that armed men were approaching the house from all sides. They were firing on all sides, leaving us entirely surrounded. And they were using all sorts of weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What sort of weapons did you see?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That's what I saw later. The first thing I saw was some sort of a Chinese machine-gun. A person who ran across the road with some sort of a pad for a weapon, he was firing most of the shots at my brother's Lada, but later I saw pistols and Kalashnikovs --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did you know -- I'll stop you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: -- as well -- as well as a whole range of semi-automatic weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did you know it was a Chinese machine-gun?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I just knew. I had been to a reserve officers' school and I took a number of classes on weapons, so I knew a little about that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, in order to better understand the testimony, you asked whether it was morning, afternoon, or evening. The witness said it was 8.00 or 9.00, but I still do not know whether it was the morning or the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was it --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Morning, morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It may have been a tad later, but it was around that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did any shots hit your house?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The walls; one came through the terrace window. When they were near the house already, a lot of grenades were thrown onto the roof. Then we heard them yelling for us to leave the house and surrender. I walked up to the door. I opened the door, and as soon as I did Zecir Nimonaj was the first to dash into the house, and then he was followed by Daut Haradinaj and another 20 or 30 of them. They searched all the rooms, and about three or four of them were hitting me in the stomach with their rifle-butts, in the veranda. One of them told my brother to lie down on the concrete floor face-down, and they continued to beat me. About 10 or 15 minutes later - hard for me to tell - one of them yelled at me, Lie face down, and he cursed my Serb mother. As soon as I was lying face down, I received several more punches and kicks but not as severe as the ones I'd received while still standing up. Then they kicked my two brothers a little, after which we were eventually taken outside the house. The house was teeming with armed men ransacking the house; however, they found nothing. Once they'd taken us outside, they continued to hit us and beat us outside the house. There were many of them involved in this. It was difficult for you to look at them. As soon as you raised your head, they would tell you immediately to keep your head down and kick you and hit you. At one point in time Nasim Haradinaj arrived, who told them, That's enough, boys. They obeyed him, and then they took us away. They were discussing for a while at first, Where should we take them? I heard them discussing this. And he said, Let's take them to HQ. I didn't know where this HQ was. I'd never seen that before. So they took us down the street, beating and mistreating us all the while, firing shots behind us.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'll ask you to pause there. I want to go back and ask you some questions about what you've just told us, then I'll come back to it; okay?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: A moment ago, you referred to -- excuse me for one moment. You said, Then they kicked my brothers a little." I heard the translation of you saying "my brothers." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Brothers -- no, not a little, quite a bit in fact but they were on the floor lying face-down. Most of the beating had occurred inside the house, however.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who -- just to clarify, you said your brothers, but before you said a cousin and your brother. Who was there? Who were they beating?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, the cousin Stijovic, there's nobody else. He's the one I'm talking about, but that's the sort of expression we use "brothers."

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you say brothers, are you referring to your brother Mijat and your cousin --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mijat Stijovic, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: If we understood the witness correct, I think that he also said the brother but his cousin Stijovic, yes. So it's not to be understood in the strict word sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: But that's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What were these people who -- the armed people who came to your house wearing?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You mean their clothes or their weapons?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Their clothes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Camouflage. All different sorts but most of them were in camouflage. Daut Haradinaj, for example, was wearing a black uniform and Zecir Nimonaj as well. There were some who were wearing camouflage trousers and a civilian top, a civilian shirt on top, but plenty of them were actually in camouflage. Most, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What language were they speaking?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, we've got --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: When speaking about the Albanian language, as you made before this -- this observation about the accent from the Albanian -- Albanians were -- was it Kosovo language or Albanian language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They used the Kosovar accent, but it's not that different, really.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was the accent -- the Kosova accent, was it a local one or another type of accent which these people were using?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Local, those villages in the area. There is a very tiny difference between the different accents.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said they said they would take you to HQ. You didn't know where it was, you'd never been there before, so they took us down the streets beating and mistreating us while firing shots behind us?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I had been there before, but it was never anybody's HQ. This was Smajl Haradinaj's family home, the place they eventually took us to. Another one of my neighbours, I knew him well, I socialised with all those people and that sort of thing. I never realised there was an HQ there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did you get there? When you say "you," are you referring to the three of you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And how did you get there? How did they take you there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: We walked. We walked as far as the house, and the distance must be between 1500 and 1800 metres, roughly speaking. Armed people were coming out on either side of the road, and again there were beatings. People would just run up to us and kick us, firing shots past our heads, and they just kept on mistreating us all the way, as far as the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you know any of these armed people?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Most of those people were my neighbours from Glodjane, from Rznic, and those other villages in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And if you look at the map which is still in front of you, are you able to locate on this map where it was you were taken to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It's very difficult. I find it very difficult to use this map. If you showed me photographs of the village, for example, I'd be able to pin-point the locations for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'll do that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
