utterances.text: If you could -- if the witness could please be shown 65 ter Exhibit 1133.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, you've done with the map so that it can be saved now so that -- it will be saved anyway, but of course markings -- every new episode of marking creates a new exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Oh, I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's move on. If you've done with the map then we get the next exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that there's a possibility to keep the old number when new markings are made, but. Madam Registrar, the number would be ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number P32, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There's a photograph on the screen in front of you, Mr. Stojanovic. Do you recognise that photograph?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we just zoom in slightly, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: You mean the photograph or the village on the photograph to be recognised?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I really mean the village. Your Honour is quite correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you recognise the village?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it does look somewhat different but -- can I have a look, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: I take this is taken from the air?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are certain buildings in this photograph that weren't around while I still resided in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Which village is in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I think this is Glodjane.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you see the house in there belonging to Smajl Haradinaj which was described to you as the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It's the fourth house along the road into Glodjane, but I can't find it in this photograph. It's to the right of my own house, which is Dubrava.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. If you can't see it on that photograph I will -- we'll move on?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What -- what happened when you got to that house?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When we got to that house, I was the first to be taken to a room inside that house, a small room. Me and the two brothers, but they left the two of them outside in a small corridor, and I was taken into the room to be sort of interrogated.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can I ask you to pause. How many floors did this house have?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Two.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was the room you were taken to on the top floor or the bottom floor?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Top floor. It's a very small room. There's a hallway just outside, and then there's a door off that -- there's the guest-room off that hallway, there's a door there. Then there's a gate and then there's a staircase, too, which takes you directly to that guest-room.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who took you to the room on the top floor?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That lad, Besnik, Rasim's son; Zecir Nimonaj; and Daut. They were the group that took us upstairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What happened when you got upstairs?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The two brothers were left to wait outside in the hall under guard, and I was taken into that room. In the meantime, one of them came out -- two, actually. Rasim's son stayed on his own, and he started questioning me. He was taunting me, trying to rile me, trying to abuse me. How many policemen were there in Decani, why was I in the village, why didn't I apply for a permit from them, that sort of thing. That's the sort of thing he was asking. He was just trying to give me grief, to mistreat me, because as a matter of fact there was nothing he could possibly ask me about. After that he offered me some coffee. He said, If you like sharing a cup of coffee? And I said, Sure, of course. And then he kept talking to me and he said, Listen, neighbour, you remember the first time we pulled you over - and I did remember that - and he said, The first time around, we did not mistreat you. I kept silent. I refrained from commenting, and then I was brought some coffee a little later. I just started to drink my coffee, but after the very first sip I got violently sick. I started choking, and I pleaded with him to open the window. He opened the door, and I could no longer hold it back. They chucked me out of the room. I was losing consciousness and choking all the time. They chucked me out into the hallway, where I fainted. This was the first time I fainted.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. I'll ask you to pause there for one moment. You described earlier in your own house being beaten. Did you sustain any injuries at that point when you were beaten in your home?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I hadn't actually felt anything until the time I arrived back, and that was a result of the blows that I had taken in the house when they were hitting me with their rifle-butts and kicking me with their pistol. My pancreas was ruptured in two places, the walls of my stomach, my colon, and a number of other injuries that I sustained which required surgery, which I eventually underwent in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'll just go back to when you were in the room, you said: "Rasim's son stayed on his own and he started questioning me." What's Rasim's son's name?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Besnik, I think, but I can't be positive.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This is Rasim's son.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was he wearing when --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Eljmi's brother. He was wearing black clothes, so was Daut and Zecir Nimonaj, the three of them. He had the insignia of the Kosovo Liberation Army on his right shoulder with a writing in Albanian -- on his left shoulder strap.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you describe the black clothes. What sort of black clothes were they?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Black clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: There's a cap -- no, no, no, more like military. Black cap with a red sign, two-headed eagle down the middle, and then in yellow letters the Albanian words for "Kosovo Liberation Army."

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can the Exhibit P9 please be displayed to the witness in e-court?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: While that's coming up -- something will be coming up on the screen in a moment, I wanted to ask you: Were these people armed when they were questioning you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: They were armed. The insignia they displayed on the cap and on the uniform, on the sleeve. They were armed. Some had the full kit, an automatic weapon and pistol, some. Mostly automatic weapons. There were elderly people not wearing a uniform, my old neighbours, and they had the old M-48 rifles, including some who were carrying semi-automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Two things here. When they were questioning you -- the two people were questioning you in the room, were those two people armed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: There were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... wasn't the witness describing one person instead of two?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If I misheard, I correct myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Whoever was questioning you --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Three took me inside and two went out, and then one remained, and then later on there were three of them again.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- were those three people armed when they were questioning you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were, but there was a table. This was a small room -- this was a small room.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I think I might have jumped slightly ahead then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, he said: "Three took me inside, two went out, and then one remained, and then later on there were three of them again." And then in your --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The brothers, three, three of them beat them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, the first question would be whether all three of them questioned the witness. That's --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I understand -- I understand. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I will take it step by step.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And I apologise --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether we could take it step by step, if I look at the clock there's not much time left to --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The only thing I want the witness to do is to identify that exhibit which is on the screen now, if he could. That was the only thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Witness, Mr. Stojanovic, in front of you, there's a --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This is the sort of emblem used by the Kosovo Liberation Army. They wore this on their caps and on their sleeves, their left hand -- left arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The witness is referring to Exhibit P9 which is displayed before him. Let the record reflect that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stojanovic, we -- it's 7.00, we stop for today. We'll like to see you back Monday at quarter past 2.00, and I'll ask now Madam Usher to escort you out of the courtroom -- oh, yes, one second, please. I want to instruct you that you speak with no one about your testimony, the testimony you have given today or the testimony still to be given on Monday perhaps. So you should not speak with anyone about it. Madam Usher. Mr. Re, I think we still -- you still owe us a date for the filing of the corrected version of the 92 bis motion. You earlier said that you had to make some inquiries and I asked you then to come back to it later today.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could I say Tuesday again with this one?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes, although it's just oral information which you were seeking this afternoon. So if you could provide it on Monday, that would be fine, but if there's -- or do you say Tuesday will be the day of the filing?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, Tuesday will be the day of the filing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can I also advise you I think I'm on track to finish within the time -- the time which we indicated, the hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm pretty much -- I don't think I'll be much -- maybe by a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then I take it that there's no difficulty to cross-examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No difficulties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we adjourn and we'll adjourn until Monday, the 26th of March, quarter past 2.00 in the afternoon, Courtroom II.
